question: What is the meaning of conditional monitoring in relation to remanufacturing?
description: Conditional monitoring in relation to remanufacturing involves providing real-time data that enables the early identification of wear and tear on products. This allows for scheduling remanufacturing before significant degradation occurs, preserving the product value.

references.text:
Continuous conditional 
monitoring provides real-time data for informing remanufacturing de­
cisions, enabling the early identification of wear and tear to preserve 
product value by scheduling remanufacturing before significant degra­
dation (Zhang, M. et al., 2022). Access to detailed disassembly in­
structions reduces the resources required to disassemble products, 
ensuring components are recovered safely and intact for remanu­
facturing (Soh et al., 2014). Predicting the return of products for 
remanufacturing is important for better planning and resource alloca­
tion, helping manage inventory, anticipating material availability, and 
ensuring a steady supply of products for remanufacturing (Goltsos et al., 
2019).
3.3. Benefits of DPPs for recycle strategies
DPPs enhance recycling efficiency by tracking product material 
composition and recyclability. By providing access to data regarding 
what materials are used and their potential for recyclability, DPPs 
enable recyclers to identify and segregate materials more accurately and 
efficiently, thereby improving the overall efficiency of recycling oper­
ations (Adisorn et al., 2021). This targeted approach minimizes waste 
and maximizes the recovery of valuable materials (Berg et al., 2022). 
Furthermore, DPPs can support the implementation of intelligent waste 
management systems. These systems leverage the detailed product data 
contained within DPPs to optimize waste materials’ sorting, processing, 
and recycling (Chauhan, A. et al., 2021; Chauhan, C. et al., 2022). By 
integrating DPP data with smart waste management technologies, 
stakeholders can streamline recycling workflows, reduce operational 
costs, and enhance the quality of recycled outputs (Gligoric et al., 2019). 
DPPs provide product information, including material compositions, 
dismantling procedures, and end-of-life handling protocols. This infor­
mation is central for recyclers and waste management professionals, as it 
informs the best practices for dismantling and processing products at the 
end of their lives (Ducuing and Reich, 2023). By understanding the 
specific requirements for handling each product, recyclers can minimize 
environmental impacts and increase the efficiency of recycling processes 
(Kristoffersen et al., 2020). The improvement of recycling processes 
through DPPs is a significant advancement. By ensuring that all stake­
holders have access to detailed and accurate product information, DPPs 
facilitate better decision-making and operational practices (Gong et al., 
2022). This leads to more effective recycling methodologies, higher 
material recovery rates, and reduced contamination of recyclable 
streams (Khan, S. A. R. et al., 2021).
3.3.1. Data needs for recycle strategies
Advancing the recycling strategy within the CE necessitates under­
standing several critical data points, each contributing to optimizing 
recycling processes. This integration of knowledge ensures the sustain­
ability of recycling operations and enhances their efficiency, thereby 
promoting a more effective CE. The foundation of effective recycling lies 
in the detailed knowledge of material composition. Understanding the 
exact materials of a product allows for the appropriate recycling 
methods to be applied, ensuring materials are recovered efficiently and 
sustainably (Bisinella et al., 2017). Coupled with this, the recyclability 
of materials plays an important role in determining the life cycle po­
tential of materials used in products. Identifying highly recyclable ma­
terials promotes their selection in design processes and guarantees that 
end-of-life products are directed toward suitable recycling pathways, 
minimizing waste (Kanwal et al., 2021). Navigating the complex land­
scape of local and global recycling regulations is necessary for main­
taining compliance and optimizing recycling rates. These regulations 
dictate the proper handling, transportation, and processing of re­
cyclables, underscoring the importance of regulatory knowledge in 
facilitating global recycling efforts (Salmenper¨a, 2021).
Moreover, product return guidelines are essential for reintegrating 
products into recycling. Companies can enhance product recycling rates 
by outlining consumer return processes and fostering greater consumer 
participation in CE strategies (Malmgren and M¨otsch Larsson, 2020). 
Disassembly instructions are essential for efficiently dismantling prod­
ucts, a step critical for recovering valuable materials.
